youtube_title: Who Pays Tariffs? The Importer, Not the Other Country
youtube_description:
Who pays tariffs? By U.S. law, the importer of record owes the duty to U.S. Customs and Border Protection, not the country that made the goods.
The importer can pass that cost on as higher prices, absorb it as lower profit, or the foreign seller can cut its price. Studies of the 2018 tariffs found foreign sellers mostly didn't cut prices, and most studies of the 2025 tariffs found U.S. buyers carried about 90% of the cost.
